title: Flashcard deck
description: The contract between Claude's extraction pass and the renderer. All three card types are fixed here from the start so that implementing a type later is never a breaking schema change.

id.description: Stable deck identifier. Keys the browser-side progress store as fc:<id>:v1, so it must stay the same across re-renders of the same deck.

title.description: Human-readable deck title, shown in the player.

source.description: Where the cards were extracted from: a file path, a URL, or a short description.

cards.description: Card ids must be unique within the deck. Uniqueness is enforced by the validator, not expressible here.

nonEmptyString.description: At least one non-whitespace character. A whitespace-only value would render as a blank card face.

slug.description: Lowercase kebab-case. Safe to use as a storage key and a DOM id.

hint.description: Optional nudge, hidden until the learner asks for it. Requesting a hint is recorded so the review screen can separate 'knew it' from 'needed a hint'.

explanation.description: Optional reasoning shown after the card is answered.

card.description: Discriminated by the 'type' field. The validator branches on 'type' before checking anything else, so a bad type yields one clear error instead of three failed branches.

basicCard.description: Prompt on the front, answer on the back. The learner reveals the answer and grades themselves.

mcqCard.description: Multiple choice. Exactly one choice is correct; that rule is enforced by the validator. Choice order is shuffled at render time, so the position of the correct answer is never learnable.

choices.description: Two choices expresses a true/false card; there is no separate type for it. Three to five is the usual range.

clozeCard.description: Fill in the blank. The prompt carries {{1}}, {{2}} ... placeholders; placeholder {{n}} is answered by blanks[n-1]. The validator checks that every placeholder has a blank and every blank has a placeholder.

prompt.description: Must contain at least one {{n}} placeholder. Numbering starts at 1, because {{n}} is answered by blanks[n-1] and {{0}} would have nothing to map to.

alternatives.description: Other spellings accepted as correct, for whichever answering mode the cloze card ends up using.
